title: The arms race
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:35Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank card covers the arms race and the idea of mutual destruction, but it is broader than this point: it adds the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis and the arms control treaties, and its question b tests that crisis, so it does not fit this point exactly.

draft.title: The arms race
card: The United States tested the first atomic bomb in 1945 and used it on Japan. The Soviet Union tested its own in 1949, and each side then built more and better weapons.
This competition is the arms race. Each superpower feared falling behind, so every gain by one side pushed the other to match it.
Both sides came to hold enough nuclear weapons to destroy the other even after being attacked first. This led to the idea of mutually assured destruction (MAD).
Under MAD, starting a nuclear war would mean destroying yourself as well. Supporters argued this fear helped deter a direct attack.
draft.remember: Each side matched the other's weapons, until a first strike meant its own destruction too.

a.q: What does mutually assured destruction mean?
opts: Each side could destroy the other even after being hit
Only the side that strikes first would be destroyed
One side held weapons that the other could not match
Both sides agreed to destroy their weapons together
a.why: MAD rests on both sides keeping enough weapons to hit back after an attack, so neither could win a nuclear war. It is not an agreement to disarm, because both sides kept and built weapons.
a.clue: Think about what happens to the attacker as well.

b.q: A student says the Soviet Union built more nuclear weapons after 1949 only because it wanted to attack the United States. Which reply fits the arms race best?
opts: Each side feared falling behind, so it matched the other
Each side built weapons only after the other had used them
Each side built weapons to settle a shared border dispute
Only one side built weapons while the other held back
b.why: The arms race was driven by fear of falling behind, so each gain by one side led the other to match it. It was not a one-sided build-up, and the weapons were not built only in response to being used.
b.clue: Think about how each side reacted to the other's gains.

a.best: Each side could destroy the other even after being hit

b.best: Each side feared falling behind, so it matched the other
